accordions.heading: What does Core 4 test for?
accordions.content: Core 4 screens for four STIs: chlamydia, gonorrhoea, HIV and syphilis. All four can cause no noticeable symptoms. Chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis can be cured with antibiotics, while HIV can be effectively managed with treatment.

accordions.heading: Is this for you?
accordions.content:
You don’t need to have symptoms to test. All four infections can cause no noticeable symptoms.

It may be worth testing if:
accordions.after: Had a possible HIV exposure in the last 72 hours? Don’t wait for a test result. Contact a sexual health clinic or go to A&E as soon as possible and ask about PEP, medication that can help prevent HIV after exposure.
checklist: You have a new sexual partner, or more than one
A sexual partner has told you they have an STI
You’ve had possible symptoms, such as unusual discharge, pain when peeing, a sore or a rash
You want to check for four STIs in one go

how.heading: How do the tests work?
how.intro:
Your bundle includes three tests for four infections. Chlamydia and gonorrhoea are checked using a swab, while HIV and syphilis are checked using finger-prick blood samples.

Each test gives a result in around 15 minutes, with no samples to send to a laboratory.

steps.title: Take your swab
steps.text: Collect your swab, mix it with the test liquids and add the prepared sample to both wells on the chlamydia and gonorrhoea test pad.

steps.title: Prick your finger
steps.text: Clean your fingertip and use a lancet to prick your finger. Add the required blood and test liquid to the HIV and syphilis test pads.

steps.title: Read your results
steps.text: Leave the test pads flat and read each result at the time shown in its instructions. The tests have slightly different reading windows.

windows.heading: When should I test?
windows.subheading: Testing too early can give a negative result even if you have an infection.

questions.question: Do I have to take all the tests at once?
questions.answer:
No. Each test is separate, so you can take them together or at different times.

An early negative may need repeating: chlamydia and gonorrhoea at 2 weeks, syphilis at 12 weeks, and HIV at 90 days.

questions.question: It’s been less than 72 hours since I may have been exposed to HIV. What should I do?
questions.answer:
If you think you may have been exposed to HIV in the last 72 hours, contact a sexual health clinic or go to A&E immediately and ask about PEP, medication that can help prevent HIV infection after exposure.

Don't wait to take a rapid HIV test or rely on a negative result. HIV can take weeks to show up on a test. PEP must be started within 72 hours, and the sooner, the better.

questions.question: How reliable are these rapid tests?
questions.answer: Rapid tests can be reliable when used correctly. Testing too early or collecting a sample incorrectly can affect your result. A negative result may need repeating if you tested early, and a positive result should be followed up with a sexual health clinic.

questions.question: What if a result is positive?
questions.answer: Contact a sexual health clinic for further testing and treatment if needed. Chlamydia, gonorrhoea and syphilis can be cured with antibiotics, and HIV treatment is highly effective. NHS sexual health services are free and confidential. If an infection is confirmed, recent sexual partners may also need to be tested.

questions.question: I’ve had syphilis before. Can I use this bundle?
questions.answer:
Yes, but the syphilis test may still show a positive result even after successful treatment, because syphilis antibodies can remain in your blood.

Speak to a sexual health clinic about the right syphilis test for you.

questions.question: Does the swab test check the throat or bottom?
questions.answer: No. The chlamydia and gonorrhoea test only checks a swab from the vagina or the urethra. If you've had oral or anal sex, speak to a sexual health clinic about testing those areas.

questions.question: Can I use this bundle while pregnant?
questions.answer: If you’re pregnant and concerned about STIs, speak to your midwife, GP or a sexual health clinic. HIV and syphilis testing is routinely offered during pregnancy through the NHS, and they can test for chlamydia and gonorrhoea safely.

questions.question: Will anyone know what I ordered?
questions.answer: No. Your order arrives in plain, discreet packaging, with nothing on the outside to reveal what’s inside. Your bank statement will also not show “Test Discreet” or the name of the test.

questions.question: Can I return my test?
questions.answer:
You can return unopened kits within 14 days of delivery. For health and hygiene reasons, we can’t take a kit back once its seal is broken.

If there’s a problem with your order or your test arrives damaged, contact us and we’ll help.
